nodes.label: One-handed signs leave the unused hand channel at zero motion energy
nodes.norm_label: one-handed signs leave the unused hand channel at zero motion energy
nodes.rationale: Video 2234689254 ('radio') shows left_hand RMS speed flat at zero throughout the clip while pose and right_hand carry the motion signal, confirming one-handed signs leave the unused hand's landmarks static/NaN-zeroed rather than noisy.

nodes.label: Z-axis dominates measured motion energy for pose landmarks
nodes.norm_label: z-axis dominates measured motion energy for pose landmarks
nodes.rationale: On a 50-video sample (seed 42), comparing xyz vs xy-only RMS speed: pose sub-groups derive 66-99% of their measured motion energy from the z axis (head 99%, hand pts 85%, legs 95%, arms 93%, hips 66%), while face/left_hand/right_hand derive only 14-24% from z — evidence that z is mostly noise for pose landmarks, motivating dropping/deprioritizing z when building landmark subsets such as ME-126.

nodes.label: ME_126 subset tops global-classification probe accuracy
nodes.norm_label: me_126 subset tops global-classification probe accuracy
nodes.rationale: Across a landmark-subset probe leaderboard (global 250-class task and 10-class scope-B task), ME_126 (126 landmarks) ranks highest on global probe balanced accuracy (~0.49), while FULL_543 (all 543 landmarks) ranks lowest (~0.40) on both tasks, indicating a curated subset outperforms using every landmark.

nodes.label: Pose and hand landmarks are less consistent across repeats of the same sign than face landmarks
nodes.norm_label: pose and hand landmarks are less consistent across repeats of the same sign than face landmarks
nodes.rationale: Across 10 videos of sign 'better', face landmarks show coefficient-of-variation of xy RMS speed clustered around 0.5-0.6, while pose and hand landmarks show much higher and more scattered CV (up to ~1.35), indicating face motion is far more repeatable across performers of the same sign than pose/hand motion.

nodes.label: Hand and pose landmarks carry far more class-discriminative information than face landmarks
nodes.norm_label: hand and pose landmarks carry far more class-discriminative information than face landmarks
nodes.rationale: Per-landmark mutual information (max over descriptors) for the 10-class scope-B task shows face landmarks clustered near MI 0.02-0.07, while left_hand/right_hand reach 0.17-0.27 and pose reaches up to ~0.20 — hands and pose are far more informative for sign classification than face, despite face being the most temporally consistent group.

nodes.label: Insight: face/lips landmarks are nearly static
nodes.norm_label: insight: face/lips landmarks are nearly static
nodes.rationale: The face landmark group (~468 points) shows RMS speed near 0.000-0.008, orders of magnitude below pose/hands, consistent with most facial landmarks contributing little motion signal for the 'beside' sign and supporting selective subsetting of landmarks (e.g. lips/eyes/nose only) rather than using all face points.

nodes.label: Insight: pose landmarks show highest motion variance
nodes.norm_label: insight: pose landmarks show highest motion variance
nodes.rationale: Bar chart of mean+/-std RMS speed grouped pose->left_hand->right_hand->face for sign 'beside' over 310 videos shows pose landmarks (indices ~8-20, upper-body arm/shoulder region) reach RMS speed up to ~0.18, far exceeding left_hand (~0.02-0.06) and right_hand (~0.015-0.05), motivating investigation of which channels/landmarks carry real signal vs noise.

nodes.label: ME-126 Landmark Subset (data source for this chart)
nodes.norm_label: me-126 landmark subset (data source for this chart)

nodes.label: 15 Worst-Performing Sign Classes (ME-126 GRU)
nodes.rationale: Lowest per-class accuracy (roughly 0.31-0.52) on the ME-126 canonical GISLR eval concentrates on signs such as give, nap, beside, there, mouth, vacuum, awake, open, that, look, pajamas, go, wake, jeans, fast - plausibly abstract/function-like or less visually distinct signs, contrasted against a broad, right-skewed distribution across 250 signs where most classes cluster in the 0.6-0.9 range.

nodes.label: Landmark Motion Profile by Body Region
nodes.norm_label: landmark motion profile by body region
nodes.rationale: Mean RMS speed per landmark, plotted across the pose/left_hand/right_hand/face landmark groups, shows pose and hand landmarks carry substantial motion (RMS speed up to ~0.13-0.15) while face landmarks are nearly static (~0.003-0.005). This motivates treating face landmarks as low-information for motion-based features and focusing model capacity on hands/pose, consistent with the ME-126 subset rationale (z channel mostly noise for pose landmarks) documented for 2026-07-15/2026-07-16.

nodes.label: Cross-Scope Sampling Consistency Finding
nodes.rationale: The global, per_category_sample, and per_video_sample RMS-speed curves overlay almost exactly across all landmarks, indicating the per-landmark motion statistic is stable regardless of which sampling scope (whole dataset vs. category subsample vs. video subsample) is used to estimate it, validating cheaper sampled analyses as a proxy for the full dataset.
